blocks.x: ultimate success. After three years of patient experimenting, Morehouse was able to present his N'goma drums to the music world and public at large. Aside from the fact that N'goma drums are an important innovation to jazz music, they have immense possibilities in symphonic music, according to Irving Mills, music impressario and Morehouse's manager. Said Mills, "It is not unreasonable to believe that the N'goma drums can be used to great advantage in symphony orchestras. A slight increase in the sizes will eliminate the current practice of tuning one kettledrum to desired tones. Several important figures in symphonic circles are preparing to try them this fall in the belief that they will be practical." Chauncey Morehouse, who may some day go down in musical history along with other instrumental inventors such as the Frenchman Sachs, began his music career as a swing drummer in the early twenties. He made numerous recordings in the Halycon days of phonograph record sales with such outstanding swingsters as Benny Goodman, Tommy Dorsey, Jean Goldkette, Red Nichols and the late jazz idol, Bix Beiderbecke. His reputation in the radio studios today is evidenced by the fact that he was recently performing with six different bands each week. He has played with Nat Schilkret, Peter Van Steeden, Don Vorhees and a dozen more.
